sub_agendas_items.title: 9-1-1 Annual Report for 2024
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
In the absence of General Manager Ryan Perrault, Mr. Roger Chapman, Director, By-law and Regulatory Services, Emergency and Protective Services Department (EPSD) introduced Ms Beth Gooding, Director, Public Safety Service, EPSD, who in turn introduced Mr. Eric Janus, Operations Manager, Ottawa Police Service. Ms Gooding and Mr. Janus spoke to a slide presentation overview of the report and responded to members’ questions. A copy of the presentation is held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.
Written correspondence was received from Mr. Michael Wood, and is held on file with the Office of the City Clerk. At the conclusion of questions to staff and Committee discussions, the report recommendation was put before Committee and was ‘Carried’, as presented.

motions.motion_text:
Report Recommendation(s)
That the Emergency Preparedness and Protective Services Committee recommend Council receive the 2024 9-1-1 annual report for information.

sub_agendas_items.title: Landscaper Regulatory Review
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Mr. Roger Chapman, Director, By-law and Regulatory Services (BLRS), Emergency and Protective Services Department (EPSD), acting on behalf of General Manager Ryan Perrault, introduced or thanked the following members of staff who had provided input into the report or were in attendance to respond to questions:
Ms Bietlot and Mr. Suatac spoke to a detailed slide presentation which served as an overview of the report.  A copy of this presentation is held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.
The Committee then heard from Mr. Jonathan Gilman, Owner, Ottawa Interlock Repair, who provided a number of slides to illustrate his points. These were saved to the SharePoint site for the Committee meeting (and are held on file with the Office of the City Clerk), having been submitted beyond the deadline for the provision of visual material. Written correspondence had also been received from Ms J.D. Devine and Mr. Jason Burggraaf, Executive Director, Greater Ottawa Homebuilders Association. Both submissions are also held on file with the Office of the City Clerk.
Following questions to the presenter and to staff, and at the conclusion of Committee discussions, the report recommendations were ‘Carried’, as presented, with Councillor I. Skalski dissenting.
Carried, with Councillor I. Skalski dissenting

sub_agendas_items.title: Ottawa Animal Care and Control By-law as Concerns the Feeding of Wildlife

motions.motion_text:
WHEREAS the City of Ottawa’s By-law Review Work Plan identifies regulatory by-laws for review or development each Term of Council; and
WHEREAS the feeding of wildlife, particularly mammalian wildlife, can result in:
WHEREAS Ottawa’s Animal Care and Control By-law currently addresses domestic animals but does not specifically regulate the feeding of wildlife; and
WHEREAS other Ontario municipalities, including Toronto, have recently introduced bans on wildlife feeding, with regulated exceptions for birds, fishing, research, animal control, and cultural practices;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that staff include a wildlife feeding by-law, or amendments to the Animal Care and Control By-law concerning the feeding of wildlife,  as an item for consideration as part of the development of next Term of Council’s By-law Review Work Plan to be approved by Council, and that other jurisdictions be considered as models as part of this work.

Inquiry: OPH and Bylaw Dog Bites Coordination
Dog bites are a rare occurrence, but when they happen residents can be confused about who to contact as both Ottawa Public Health (OPH) and Bylaw Services have webpages requesting incidents be reported through their respective organizations. The overwhelming majority of dog owners are responsible people and complainants may be motivated to reach out to OPH to report a public health concern but avoid reaching out to Bylaw to prevent escalation of consequences to the dog. Or they may be instructed by a doctor fixing their wounds to call OPH, and a Police Officer taking their case to contact Bylaw. With that in mind, could you please address the following questions.

sub_agendas_items.title: Support for the establishment of a National Fire Administration
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Chair R. Brockington, stepped out of the Chair to introduce the following Motion to add an item under “Other Business”, and he asked for the Committee’s support:
Motion No. EPPSC 2025-19-04
Moved by R. Brockington:
That the Rules of Procedure be waived to allow for the consideration of this motion by the Emergency Preparedness and Protective Services Committee at today’s meeting and by Council, at its meeting of 22 October 2025, regarding the establishment of a National Fire Administration.
Carried
Speaking to the following Motion, Councillor Brockington explained that a large number of Provincial Fire Chief Associations have expressed support to their respective Premiers for a National Fire Administration, further to which there is also currently a Private Member’s Bill before the House of Commons calling for the creation of a National Fire Administration. He further explained that such an administration would coordinate, advise, lead and support the complexity of the fire situation in Canada, as other comparator countries have done (i.e., the United States, Japan and Australia).
Motion No. EPPSC 2025-19-05
Moved by R. Brockington:
WHEREAS there are approximately 3,200 fire departments across Canada; and
WHEREAS the scale and complexity of events to which Canadian fire services are expected to respond have increased dramatically in recent years, a trend that is anticipated to continue; and
WHEREAS all levels of government in Canada are involved in various aspects of fire and emergency management; and
WHEREAS collaboration and strategic coordination among governments and fire services are essential to ensure preparedness for major emergencies and the efficient use of resources; and
WHEREAS the increasing frequency and severity of wildfires across Canada highlight the need for a coordinated and sustained national approach to prevention, mitigation, response, and recovery; and
WHEREAS a National Fire Administration, established within Public Safety Canada and developed in collaboration with Canada’s fire chiefs would serve as a coordinating mechanism for policy and decision-making on technical fire and emergency management matters, without impinging upon provincial or territorial jurisdiction; and
WHEREAS such an initiative would provide an important opportunity for provinces and territories to seek federal support in replenishing emergency equipment and ensuring that communities are adequately equipped to respond to crises; and
WHEREAS establishing a National Fire Administration would strengthen Canada’s capacity to protect homes, businesses, and the economy, while modernizing the national emergency response system;
THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED THAT the Emergency Preparedness and Protective Services Committee recommend City Council express its support for the establishment of a National Fire Administration within Public Safety Canada, developed in collaboration with Canada’s fire chiefs; and
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED THAT the City Clerk be directed to share a copy of this motion with The Honourable Gary Anandasangaree, federal Minister of Public Safety, on behalf of City Council.
Councillor S. Desroches suggested a friendly amendment to the Motion, to add the words “headquartered in Ottawa” following “…within Public Safety Canada,” in the Motion’s first operational clause, to which the mover agreed.
Chief P. Hutt, Ottawa Fire Services was present to offer support for this initiative.
At the conclusion of questions to staff and Committee discussions, Motion No. EPPSC 2025-19-05 was put before Committee and was ‘Carried’, as amended.
